questionText:
Consider a network that uses Ethernet and IPv4. Assume that IPv4 headers do not use any options field. Each Ethernet frame can carry a maximum of 1500 bytes in its data field. A UDP segment is transmitted. The payload (data) in the UDP segment is 7488 bytes.

Which ONE of the following choices has the CORRECT total number of fragments transmitted and the size of the last fragment including IPv4 header?
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

1. Calculate total IP Payload:
• UDP header size = $8\text{ bytes}$
• UDP payload = $7488\text{ bytes}$
• Total UDP segment size (which forms the IP payload) = $7488 + 8 = 7496\text{ bytes}$

2. Determine maximum IP payload per fragment:
• Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) = $1500\text{ bytes}$
• Standard IPv4 header size (without options) = $20\text{ bytes}$
• Maximum payload capacity per IP fragment = $1500 - 20 = 1480\text{ bytes}$
• Since $1480$ is a multiple of $8$ ($1480 / 8 = 185$), each non-final fragment carries $1480\text{ bytes}$ of payload.

3. Calculate total number of fragments:
• Number of full fragments = $\lfloor 7496 / 1480 \rfloor = 5$ fragments
• Payload in 5 fragments = $5 \times 1480 = 7400\text{ bytes}$
• Remaining payload for 6th fragment = $7496 - 7400 = 96\text{ bytes}$
• Therefore, total fragments = $6$.

4. Calculate size of the last fragment including IPv4 header:
• Size of 6th fragment = IP payload + IPv4 header = $96 + 20 = 116\text{ bytes}$.

Hence, the correct answer is 6 fragments, 116 bytes, corresponding to Option (D).
